identity.title: A Multifrequency Global View of Callisto's Thermal Properties from ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present thermal observations of Callisto’s leading and trailing hemispheres obtained using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.87 mm (343 GHz), 1.3 mm (233 GHz), and 3 mm (97 GHz).

question.value: What are the global thermophysical properties (thermal inertia, emissivity, electrical skin depth) and local thermal anomalies of Callisto's leading and trailing hemispheres, from multi-frequency ALMA maps?

evidence.quote: In this work, we present the first global set of high-resolution thermal observations of Callisto using ALMA by mapping the leading and trailing hemispheres at 3 mm (97 GHz), 1.3 mm (233 GHz), and 0.87 mm (343 GHz).

claims.hypothesis: Can a single thermal inertia model describe Callisto's millimeter thermal emission?
claims.experiment: Fitted single-Gamma models to each frequency and hemisphere and inspected residuals
claims.result: Single-Gamma models left systematic residuals (warm disk centre, cold limbs) in nearly every observation
claims.finding: Single-Gamma models are not sufficient; more complex models fit better

evidence.quote: It is clear that models parameterized by a single thermal inertia are not sufficient to model Callisto’s thermal emission

claims.hypothesis: Are Callisto's millimeter emissivities high compared to Europa and Ganymede?
claims.experiment: Derived emissivity from all three model treatments at 97, 233 and 343 GHz
claims.result: Emissivity 0.85-0.97 in all treatments, versus 0.75-0.85 for Europa and Ganymede
claims.finding: Callisto has consistently high millimeter emissivity

evidence.quote: We find that Callisto’s millimeter emissivities are high, with representative values of 0.85-0.97, compared to 0.75-0.85 for Europa and Ganymede at these wavelengths.

claims.hypothesis: Are local thermal anomalies tied to impact craters?
claims.experiment: Subtracted best-fit global models and compared residual cold spots with geologic features
claims.result: Cold spots of 3-5 K at Valhalla and the Adlinda/Heimdall/Lofn complex
claims.finding: Large impact features appear as cold anomalies

evidence.quote: brightness temperatures that are locally 3-5 K colder than surrounding terrain are associated with impact craters

claims.hypothesis: Do the ALMA data sense below Callisto's dark material blanket, via frequency or hemisphere differences in thermal properties?
claims.experiment: Compared best-fit thermal inertias across 97-343 GHz and between hemispheres
claims.result: No clear trend with depth and no consistent leading/trailing difference
claims.finding: ALMA may not have bypassed the dark material blanket

evidence.quote: The fact that we do not constrain a difference in Callisto’s thermal properties between 97-343 GHz leaves open the possibility that our ALMA observations have not bypassed the dark material blanket that globally covers Callisto.

claims.hypothesis: Is the L-shaped warm anomaly on the leading hemisphere seen earlier at 343 GHz real?
claims.experiment: Examined 233 and 97 GHz leading hemisphere residual maps
claims.result: Warm region reproduced at 233 GHz and in the same area at 97 GHz
claims.finding: Confirmed at additional frequencies, possibly lower thermal inertia from micrometeorite bombardment

evidence.quote: Finally, an L-shaped warm anomaly in the center of the leading hemisphere tentatively presented by (cite: camarca_thermal_2023) in the standalone 343 GHz data is confirmed at additional frequencies
